subject: Post-call recap — Clearwater Insurance: prompt/output retention & access controls
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@clearwater-ins.com>, Elena Morales <elena@clearwater-ins.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call recap — Clearwater Insurance: prompt/output retention & access controls

Hi Rajiv / Elena —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and the concrete answers/next steps you asked for around prompt/output PII handling, retention, and logging. I’ve kept this targeted to the five items you raised; if I missed anything, flag it and we’ll update.

What we reviewed (short answers):
1) Where are prompts/outputs stored?
   - Hosted (Redwood API): by default data is processed in transient memory on our serving fleet in the region you select (we recommend us-east-1 for Clearwater). We persist minimal request logs for operational debugging; those logs can be configured or disabled under a contractual data-handling addendum.
   - Dedicated / Private: customer data can be kept entirely in your VPC/on-prem and never leave your environment.

2) Retention (how long do we keep prompt/input/output artifacts?)
   - Default debugging logs: up to 7 days (rolling) for standard hosted customers; we can reduce this to 0 days (no persistent logs) for enterprise customers under contract.
   - Audit logs (metadata for billing & SLA): retained 1 year by default, configurable.

3) Access controls & encryption
   - Data at rest and in transit are encrypted (TLS + customer-managed KMS available for Dedicated/Private).
   - RBAC + role separation for access to logs; access is logged and requires justification for manual retrieval.

4) PII in outputs and prompt leakage risk
   - We recommend prompt-level redaction on client-side where feasible. For cases where you must send full customer prompts, we can enable an ephemeral-only mode that avoids writing prompt/output to disk.

5) Evidence & next steps
   - Attached: SOC2_summary.pdf (executive summary of controls).
   - Action: Jasmine to provide a short contractual paragraph for the SOW that guarantees minimal retention and region lock.

Immediate next steps:
- I will send a draft data-handling addendum (attached) and a one-paragraph statement you can include in your procurement ticket.
- Technical sync: Ben to propose a 30m follow-up to walk the security/engineering team through the Dedicated/Private options.
- Rajiv: confirm whether Clearwater needs EU-only residency or US-only.

Thanks —

Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0148

Rajiv — quick follow with the technical specifics you asked for. Short answers: 

1) "0 days" (ephemeral mode) = no prompt/output is written to persistent storage by our service in hosted mode. Data is kept in memory for the duration of the request and any in-flight KV cache; we do not materialize request text to disk. For customers that require absolute assurance, Dedicated/Private routes offer VPC-only processing and customer KMS.

2) Embeddings/vector storage: by default the API will not persist embeddings unless you call our embedding-storage endpoint or explicitly enable vector persistence. If you pass text to the embeddings endpoint without requesting storage, nothing is stored. If you use Redwood-managed vector DB (opt-in), we persist vectors per your retention setting.

3) Region lock: confirmed — we can lock Clearwater to us-east-1 for both serving and logging. This will be included in the addendum paragraph.

I'll attach the same SOC2 summary and include a one-paragraph SOW blurb in the next message.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

SOW paragraph (suggested) — copy/paste into procurement:
